gloss: apprentice; disciple; pupil in a trade

definitions.gloss: apprentice; disciple; pupil learning a trade or craft
definitions.explanation: A person learning a trade, craft, or art under the guidance of a master. Implies a traditional master-apprentice relationship where skills are passed down through hands-on training.

examples.japanese: {徒弟|とてい}{制度|せいど}で{技術|ぎじゅつ}を{学|まな}ぶ。
examples.english: To learn skills through an apprenticeship system.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}は{若|わか}い{頃|ころ}、{大工|だいく}の{徒弟|とてい}として{働|はたら}いていた。
examples.english: When he was young, he worked as a carpenter's apprentice.

examples.japanese: かつての{職人|しょくにん}の{世界|せかい}では、{徒弟|とてい}は{何年|なんねん}もかけて{親方|おやかた}から{技|わざ}を{盗|ぬす}むように{覚|おぼ}えたものだ。
examples.english: In the old world of craftsmen, apprentices would spend years learning the master's skills by watching and imitating.

notes:
A compound of {徒|と} (follower, companion) and {弟|てい} (younger person, disciple). A somewhat formal or literary word that evokes the traditional system of learning trades through direct apprenticeship under a master ({親方|おやかた} or {師匠|ししょう}).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {徒弟|とてい}{制度|せいど}: apprenticeship system
- {徒弟|とてい}{教育|きょういく}: apprentice training
- {徒弟|とてい}として{働|はたら}く: to work as an apprentice
- {徒弟|とてい}{関係|かんけい}: master-apprentice relationship

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {弟子|でし}: disciple, pupil — more general and common; used for martial arts, traditional arts, and academic mentorship
- {見習|みなら}い: trainee, intern — modern term for someone learning on the job
- {丁稚|でっち}: shop boy, young apprentice — historical term for child apprentices in merchant houses

CULTURAL NOTE:
The {徒弟|とてい}{制度|せいど} was the primary way trades were transmitted in pre-modern Japan. While formal apprenticeship has declined, its spirit survives in fields like {寿司|すし} making, {落語|らくご}, and traditional crafts, where years of training under a master are still expected.
